newsitem.title: USA: Interview - Millennium sees $100 mln savings.
newsitem.headline: Interview - Millennium sees $100 mln savings.

text.p: Millennium Chemicals Inc expects to achieve $100 million in cost savings this year, chief executive William Landuyt told Reuters.
"Since 1992, we have taken out $190 million of costs and we have earmarked another $100 million for this year," he said in a telephone interview.

Millenium, the largest producer of low density polyethylene in the U.S. and third largest producer of high density polyethylene, had seen improved prices for polyethylene this year, but he expected new capacity in the fourth quarter would cap prices until the cycle turned again in 2000 or 2001.
As for the outlook of titanium dioxide, Landuyt said price increases announced at the start of this year would stick.
"When you see all the big producers announcing rises, you can expect an improvement," he said. "Customers are on 90 days notice, so we will start to see an impact in the second quarter."
Asked if he was comfortable with analysts' forecasts of earnings per share of 25 cents for the first quarter, he said he could not comment.
